guide.summary: Private app, own workspace only (self-serve, wait none); Public app for customers' workspaces (app review); Public app listed in the App Store (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app, own workspace only (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app listed in the App Store (app review).

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Intercom, fine for prototypes. Users then see Composio's name on the consent screen, and quota is shared across Composio users.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio has a managed Intercom app. For production you will likely want your own, so users see your brand and you get dedicated quota and control over scopes.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Dedicated rate-limit quota instead of shared quota
Control over scopes beyond Composio's defaults
Shorter trigger polling intervals than the 15-minute managed minimum

prerequisites.title: Paid Intercom workspace and customer agreement
prerequisites.detail: Using the Intercom Service, even through a free platform account, requires the separate Intercom Customer Agreement. A private app only reads data from your own paid workspace.

prerequisites.title: Test account or setup instructions
prerequisites.detail: Reviewers test full functionality, so provide test credentials or setup instructions in the app description if your service needs an account.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. You can register several, including testing and production ones.

steps.title: Create app and enable OAuth
steps.detail: In the Developer Hub, tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page and fill out Redirect URLs and Permissions.
steps.done_when: client_id and client_secret are visible on the Basic Information page.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list and justifications
steps.detail: Pick only the scopes your use case needs and write a justification for each, since over-privileged scopes are the most common rejection reason.
steps.done_when: Each requested scope maps to a real feature.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Intercom app's Redirect URLs.

steps.title: Record the end-to-end video
steps.detail: Show install with OAuth (full client_id and state in the URL), all functionality, and uninstall.
steps.done_when: Video covers install, features and uninstall.

steps.title: Complete listing and partner pages
steps.detail: Fill in the App Listing, Installation status and App Partner Program pages with correctly sized images and company details.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Fill in the description and video on the Submit for a review page and click Submit for Review.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days. If rejected, fix the requested changes and resubmit.
steps.done_when: App is approved and becomes public unlisted.

steps.title: Set listing live
steps.detail: After approval, select List in App store to go live in the App Store.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes cause rejection
traps.detail: Over-privileged scopes are the most common reason for initial rejection. Intercom may also approve fewer permissions than you asked for.

traps.title: Incomplete video means resubmission
traps.detail: If the video does not show all functionality and the OAuth processes, you must resubmit it. Broken or unclear installation links also cause rejection.

blockers.symptom: Review stalls beyond seven business days
blockers.what_it_means: A 2021 community report describes a 15-day wait with no response from support.
blockers.what_to_do: Escalate through Intercom support, which handles app review requests.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the follow-up message with app name and submission date.

open_questions: Is the unlisted public path subject to any other limits or fees? Check the Intercom Developer Hub or ask Intercom support.
Do customer workspace admins need to approve or allow the app? The dossier does not say; test with a customer workspace.
What is the real current review time? Docs say up to seven business days, but only an old forum report exists; ask Intercom support.
